past_paper_mcqs.stem_text: If the volume of one cube is $1.76\text{ cm}^3$, then the volume of twenty-one such cubes rounded off to three significant figures is
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: Total volume = 21 * 1.76 = 36.96 cm³. When rounded off to 3 significant figures, 36.96 becomes 37.0 cm³.

past_paper_mcqs.explanation: Correct option according to the official board answer key.

past_paper_mcqs.stem_text: The number 123.4 can also be written in scientific notation as
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: To express 123.4 in standard scientific notation ($a \times 10^n$ where $1 \le |a| < 10$), the decimal point is moved two places to the left, giving $1.234 \times 10^2$.

past_paper_mcqs.explanation: The SI prefix for $10^{-9}$ is nano.

past_paper_mcqs.explanation: Correct option according to the official board answer key.

past_paper_mcqs.stem_text: The total number of significant figures in $0.002022$ are
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: Leading zeros to the left of the first non-zero digit ($0.00$) are only placeholders and are not significant. All four digits starting from the first non-zero digit ($2, 0, 2, 2$) are significant, giving a total of 4 significant figures.

past_paper_mcqs.stem_text: The number $0.0000509$ can be represented in scientific notation as
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: Moving the decimal point 5 places to the right to place it immediately after the first non-zero digit ($5$) gives $5.09 \times 10^{-5}$.

past_paper_mcqs.stem_text: If the volume of the given cuboid is $0.03\text{ m}^3$, then the value of $x$ will be
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: The volume of a cuboid is $V = l \times w \times h$. Substituting $V = 0.03\text{ m}^3$, $l = 0.5\text{ m}$, and $w = 0.2\text{ m}$ gives $0.03 = 0.5 \times 0.2 \times x = 0.1x$, so $x = 0.03 / 0.1 = 0.3\text{ m}$.

past_paper_mcqs.stem_text: The total number of derived quantities involved in the equation $S = v_i t + \frac{1}{2}at^2$ is
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: In the second equation of motion $S = v_i t + \frac{1}{2}at^2$, distance/displacement ($S$, length) and time ($t$) are base quantities, while initial velocity ($v_i$) and acceleration ($a$) are derived quantities — making a total of two derived quantities.

past_paper_mcqs.stem_text: A force of $10\text{ N}$ is acting on a body along x-axis. The value of its y-component will be
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: Since the force acts entirely along the x-axis ($\theta = 0^\circ$), its y-component is $F_y = F\sin 0^\circ = 10 \times 0 = 0\text{ N}$.

crqs.question: i. How many significant figures are there in 0.0102030? ii. List the rules of significant figures applied.
crqs.answer: i. 6 significant figures. ii. Leading zeros before the first non-zero digit are not significant; zeros between non-zero digits and trailing zeros in a decimal fraction are significant.
crqs.source: AKU-EB SSC-I 2025 Annual Paper II Q.1

crqs.question: Write the name of the physical quantity measured by Vernier callipers and micrometer screw gauge, along with their typical least counts.
crqs.answer: Length / internal and external diameter (Vernier callipers least count = 0.01 cm or 0.1 mm; Micrometer screw gauge least count = 0.001 cm or 0.01 mm).
crqs.source: AKU-EB SSC-I Model Paper II Q.1

crqs.question:
An online purchasing company delivered a fragile item to its customer in a triangular box. The breadth and height of the box was $15\text{ cm}$ and $20\text{ cm}$ respectively.

Calculate the volume of the triangular box upto two significant figures.

(Note: $\text{Volume }(V) = \text{Breadth} \times \text{Height}$)
crqs.question_text:
An online purchasing company delivered a fragile item to its customer in a triangular box. The breadth and height of the box was $15\text{ cm}$ and $20\text{ cm}$ respectively.

Calculate the volume of the triangular box upto two significant figures.

(Note: $\text{Volume }(V) = \text{Breadth} \times \text{Height}$)

rubric.description: 1 mark for writing the correct calculated answer: V = 15 cm × 20 cm = 300 cm² (or cm³).
1 mark for rounding and writing the answer to two significant figures: 3.0 × 10² cm².

crqs.answer:
Given Data:
Breadth ($B$) = $15\text{ cm}$
Height ($H$) = $20\text{ cm}$

Formula:
$\text{Volume }(V) = \text{Breadth} \times \text{Height}$

Calculation:
$V = 15\text{ cm} \times 20\text{ cm} = 300\text{ cm}^2$

Rounding to two significant figures:
$V = 3.0 \times 10^2\text{ cm}^2$ (where $3$ and $0$ are two significant figures).

erqs.question: Differentiate between systematic errors and random errors in physical measurements, giving two causes and one method of reducing each.
erqs.answer: Systematic errors occur consistently in one direction due to zero error of instruments or faulty calibration; reduced by applying zero correction. Random errors are unpredictable fluctuations due to parallax or environmental changes; reduced by taking the average of multiple repeated readings.

numericals.problem:
An online purchasing company delivered a fragile item to its customer in a triangular box. The breadth and height of the box was $15\text{ cm}$ and $20\text{ cm}$ respectively.

Calculate the volume of the triangular box upto two significant figures.

(Note: $\text{Volume }(V) = \text{Breadth} \times \text{Height}$)
numericals.solution:
Given Data:
Breadth ($B$) = $15\text{ cm}$
Height ($H$) = $20\text{ cm}$

Formula:
$\text{Volume }(V) = \text{Breadth} \times \text{Height}$

Calculation:
$V = 15\text{ cm} \times 20\text{ cm} = 300\text{ cm}^2$

Rounding to two significant figures:
$V = 3.0 \times 10^2\text{ cm}^2$ (where $3$ and $0$ are two significant figures).

numericals.problem: The volume of one small metallic cube is 1.76 cm³. Calculate the total volume of 21 such cubes and round the result to three significant figures.
numericals.solution: V_total = 21 × 1.76 cm³ = 36.96 cm³. Rounded to 3 significant figures, V_total = 37.0 cm³.

numericals.problem: Two forces ($9\text{ N}$ and $12\text{ N}$) act at the right angle at point O, as shown in the given figure. What will be the magnitude and direction of the resultant force?
numericals.solution: Magnitude $R = \sqrt{9^2 + 12^2} = \sqrt{81 + 144} = \sqrt{225} = 15\text{ N}$. By vector addition (head-to-tail / parallelogram law), the resultant lies along OQ.
